body:
m1: I TRACED FlowStep FOR YOU, AND IT ANSWERS YOUR OPEN SITE IN THE UNCOMFORTABLE
DIRECTION. It also qualifies three of the seven you marked safe. Two verified
structural facts, then one thing I did NOT verify and am not going to assert.

FACT 1 -- FlowStep HAS NO DOOR, AND ITS SIBLING DOES. You could not trace it to a
validating door because there is not one.

    matrix.scala:116   final class AlignmentRow private[align] (...)     sealed
    matrix.scala:295   final case class FlowStep(from, to, mass: Map[...]) CASE CLASS

AlignmentRow's own docstring says it is not a case class because "fromProduct
would mint negative or non-finite mass from any package". FlowStep carries the
same kind of payload -- a Map to Double mass -- and is a plain case class fifteen
lines away. TransitionFlow(steps) likewise. So `Mirror.fromProduct` mints a
FlowStep with NaN mass from any package, and coherenceA at signature.scala:583
sums exactly that field. This is a new instance of bd-01M17ZNXY6 in a type that
bead never named, and the pattern is the one we keep finding: somebody sealed the
type they were looking at and not its sibling.

FACT 2 -- AND THIS IS THE PART THAT TOUCHES YOUR "SAFE" SEVEN. The seal does not
validate in-package construction. The companion has TWO doors:

    private[align] def apply(unit, mass) = new AlignmentRow(unit, mass)   NO CHECK
    def of(unit, mass): Either[...]  = ... if row.isWellFormed ...        CHECKS

and the aligner uses the first one. hsmm.scala:641 reads `AlignmentRow(units(i).id,
states(i).map(...).toMap)` -- the unvalidated private apply. So "every AlignmentRow
in existence came through a validating door" holds for rows built OUTSIDE align and
not for the ones the HSMM itself produces, which are the rows the estimands are
computed from. The docstring is precise about this and I had read it as broader
than it is: it says fromProduct would mint bad mass FROM ANY PACKAGE. The seal is
an external defence. In-package construction is trusted.

That does not make :457, :469 and :493 defects. It removes the reason you gave for
them being safe, which is a different and smaller claim.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY, and where I stop. Whether NaN can actually arrive:

    hsmm.scala:638  val logZ = logSumExp(states(n-1).map(s => logAlpha(n-1)(s)))
    hsmm.scala:737  logSumExp: if xs.isEmpty then Double.NegativeInfinity
    hsmm.scala:642  math.exp(logAlpha(i)(s) + logBeta(i)(s) - logZ)

logZ can be NegativeInfinity, and -Inf minus -Inf is NaN, so exp yields NaN. That
is a structural possibility, NOT a reachability claim -- it needs every path that
can drive all alphas to -Inf, and I have not enumerated them.

Against it, there ARE existing NaN defences on this module's paths:
    hsmm.scala:269  else if logLikelihood.isNaN then Left(InconsistentResult(...))
    hsmm.scala:304  case st if st.mass.values.exists(m => m < 0.0 || m.isNaN || m.isInfinite)

:304 is exactly the check that would catch a poisoned row. I have NOT established
whether it lies on the path that feeds signature's estimands or only on another
one. That single question decides whether any of this is live, and it is the
CONSEQUENCE question from your own three-way split -- the one you wrote must be
RUN rather than predicted. I am not going to predict it.

So the honest state of bd-01M174W3D: your seven-of-eight audit stands as an audit;
the REASON for three of them needs replacing; the eighth is not merely untraced but
has no door to trace to. I would rather hand you that than a tidier answer.

Neither of us should touch align while cand-7KHF208 is pending. I have edited
nothing -- this is all `git show` against main.
